name: The list of contents: complete, nothing twice, nothing missed
summary: I ran a full house through the real Name N shots button on a frozen copy: a 706 probate estate with two representatives, 8 rooms and 31 Items photos seeded with the usual mistakes. The pipeline itself works well. One press named, room-checked and valued 50 lines, restore kept the item number, and the desk drew 400 lines in about 90 ms. But the desk cannot yet prove the list is complete, and it does not stop an incomplete list from going out as final. With every line valued and the appraisals waived, the Court Inventory printed FINAL with both adoption lines while the same page listed the coin collection twice ($6,000), the car twice, 16 chairs for 8, the lamps in two rooms and two open duplicate groups. At that moment 0 of 51 lines were reviewed and all 8 rooms were unlocked. Desk-side, the TC got no warning: Possible duplicates cannot see a walkthrough collection or vehicle line (they have no room). Not duplicates silences a line for good, so a later real double of it was stamped but never shown. Rooms with no lines appear on no paper and no screen. The package's gap question ignores unnamed lines, and a must-find can be ticked Found without naming any item. For the reader: the schedules a PR adopts have no item numbers, rooms or photo references, so they cannot be tied to the ledger, receipts or photos. On a 706 estate, a qty-1 mixed group (a $1,800 jewelry box) escapes the $100 lot test while the worklist prints a clearance. One finding is urgent and outside the papers: a single snapshot of a 400-line house puts the job record at 58,402 characters. That is past the Jobs sheet's 50,000-character cell, so job saves from that device fail from then on and the Jobs tab may be cleared. The fix to the papers is one completeness reader, room by room and job-wide, driving a "ready for counsel" card, the schedules' DRAFT reasons, the package's gap question and a printed rooms index. Alongside it the agents can take on the matching work: walkthrough collections and vehicles in Agent One's context, and the room check reporting objects no line names. A text pass across the whole house would cover the pairs the 12-photo window misses.
works_well: One press of Name N shots ran naming, the room check and Agent Two in a line with no further press (run1.js: agentIdentify x2, agentRoomCheck, agentValue x3; 31 photographs became 50 named and valued lines, 18 of them split off frames).

Restore gives a removed line back under its own number (run5.js: lamps #2 removed and restored as #2); numbers are never reissued and collisions resolve the same way on every device (_invAssignItemNos).
Possible duplicates shows both photographs side by side with the room check's plain sentence and a confidence word; Remove or Not duplicates is two presses (run6.js).
The Court Inventory and Trust Schedule refuse FINAL and withhold the signature block while any line is unvalued or pending appraisal, and name the floor's lines (out1/court.html: '#23 unnamed').
The As-Found Record names a room in scope with no as-found photographs (out2/asfound.html: Hall Closet).
The living Contents Record states its own gaps (out7/contents.html: 50 undecided, 1 photographed item not named, 1 with no photograph).
MAIV aggregate (§20.2031-6(b)) and the Lots to split chip and worklist block compute per-article figures and say plainly that an average can hide an article over the cap.
A whole house is fast at the desk: renderInventoryTab 81-103 ms at 400 lines, agentDuplicateGroups 1 ms (run10.js).
Bulk Remove lines confirms once and names the first eight lines (run8.js).
measurements: Snapshot size (run3.js): 400 named lines; one More > Snapshot took the job record from 1,344 to 58,402 characters (142.6 per line). The next saveAllJobs payload was 62,106 characters, against the 50,000-character cell cap (main-sync.gs:615).

Room check coverage (window.js, the server's _arWindows of 12 photographs overlapping by 6): share of photo pairs in one room ever read together is 100% at 12 photos, 80% at 16, 61% at 24, 38% at 40, 27% at 60.
Desk render (run10.js, 400 lines, page.evaluate timing): renderInventoryTab 103, 82, 81 ms; agentDuplicateGroups 1 ms; 28 same-name groups, 8 shown at a time.
Removing a 'nothing to list' line (run4.js C, real controls): 4 presses (Unnamed shots chip, the row's open arrow, Remove line, confirm).
Folding a drawer Agent One listed as 12 lines back to one (run8.js): 13 presses (11 ticks, Remove lines, confirm), plus retyping and re-valuing the survivor.

FINAL Court Inventory over a double-counted list (run4.js E, out4/court-final.html): total $37,340, including about $3,800 in second copies (coin $3,000, car $800; plus a lot of 8 chairs and 8 single chairs, $1,600 + $1,600).

Pipeline (run1.js): 31 Items photographs became 50 live lines: 48 named by Agent One, 18 split lines, 1 'nothing to list', 1 auto collection line. Possible duplicates showed 0 groups with the stub room check.
Package gap question before naming (run8.js): ['8 rooms not yet locked','1 line with no disposition'] with 31 lines unnamed.
Snapshot comparison after a count change on an appraised line (run5.js): 'Items 50 → 50 … Unchanged 50'.
verifier_note: The report is reliable. I rebuilt the core claims on my own fixture: a 706 probate estate with two representatives, 7 rooms, 12 unnamed Items shots, a walkthrough coin collection, a vehicle and must-finds (INV-verify/vseed.js). I drove it through the real controls: Name N shots, Remove line, Add →, the row's Total and Qty boxes, Waive, More ▾ > Court Inventory, Snapshot, Not duplicates and + Another item. Every defect, inconsistency and accuracy claim I could drive reproduced: INV-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07, 08, 11, 14, 18 and 21. I confirmed the rest from the code and prompt lines. Where I re-rated, it was down: INV-03, 06, 09, 10 and 11 are less severe than filed. INV-03 has a visible row chip and a built join (Use that line); its detection is what is missing. The auditor's jewelry-box case for INV-09 contradicts Agent One's own prompt, which gives jewelry a line of its own. INV-13 is the Open work item from P24. INV-23 is against the decided no-agent-on-as-found rule. INV-12 is accurate, but it pulls against Anthony's 'no bunch of flags'. A sibling I found: a walkthrough collection or vehicle line with no photograph prints condition 'as photographed' on the Court Inventory, a false statement on a court paper (v2.log coin and Jaguar rows). Folded into INV-03 and INV-04. Logs are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/INV-verify/.

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 in part (P8, its critical part: an open possible duplicate keeps the Court Inventory and the Trust Schedule DRAFT and is named on them and the Estate Inventory Report; tests/p8-nothing-twice.test.js, browser step 123). Open: the walkthrough collection and the vehicle listed twice with no group shown (INV-03, INV-04), for P8's later build
findings.title: The Court Inventory and Trust Schedule print FINAL with adoption lines over a list that double counts
findings.where: More ▾ > Court Inventory / Trust Schedule. printCourtInventory havellin.html:34030-34112 (FINAL is decided at 34112 from the pending appraisals, unvalued lines and the matter only); printTrustSchedule 34219-34265 (same rule). Neither carries _invProgressStamp (only _avUnreviewedStamp at 34150 / 34283).
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/INV/run4.js, section E; page saved as INV/out4/court-final.html. Setup: every line given a value and the four pending appraisals waived. Status read 'FINAL 48 values not yet reviewed', with a 'Reviewed and adopted by' line for each personal representative and a total of $37,340. The same page lists: 'Coin collection … $3,000' and 'Coin collection in three blue albums … $3,000'; 'Mercedes-Benz SL500 … $14,000' and 'Mercedes SL500 … $800'; 9 dining-chair rows (a lot of 8 plus 8 single chairs); 'Brass table lamps with pleated shades' twice. At the same moment probatePackageGaps said ['8 rooms not yet locked','51 lines with no disposition'] and 0 of 51 lines were reviewed. INV/run6.js: still FINAL with two room-check duplicate groups open (sofa 'plainly one thing', chairs 'very likely'). The Estate Inventory Report from the same state was stamped 'IN PROGRESS — 0 of 50 items reviewed'.
findings.tc_impact: Nothing on the desk or the page tells the TC the schedule is not ready; the IN PROGRESS stamp they see on the Estate Inventory Report is missing on the paper the PR signs. The PR adopts a §733.604 schedule that overstates the estate by several thousand dollars and counts one sofa, one collection and one car twice; the attorney finds the doubles or the court does.
findings.proposal: One DOM-free reader, inventoryCompleteness(jobId, job, all) (see INV-06). Its blocking set goes onto _draftWhy/_draftFix in both printers, e.g. 'DRAFT — 2 possible duplicates open · 1 walkthrough collection may be listed twice · 2 rooms not locked · 3 photographs not named'. The set: open Possible duplicates groups, unshot collection or vehicle lines with a likely photographed twin, nothing-to-list lines, unnamed lines, rooms in scope not locked. Both schedules carry _invProgressStamp as the Estate Inventory Report does. The page still prints; only the adoption block is withheld, which is the existing DRAFT rule. The Closing bar's line reads the same reader. Agent Two could hold lines in an open duplicate group out of the automatic value run until a person resolves them; today both copies are valued.
findings.decided_conflict: 'Review gates nothing; documents in progress are stamped IN PROGRESS and never withheld': the proposal keeps every paper printable and uses the schedules' existing DRAFT rule (signature withheld), never a block on the print.
findings.vnote: Reproduced on my own fixture through the real controls. Name 12 shots ran naming, the room check and Agent Two. Then Remove line on the nothing-to-list row, Add → on the vehicle panel with 6000 typed in its Total, and the guardrail's two Waive presses. More ▾ > Court Inventory then opened in the viewer reading 'FINAL 11 values not yet reviewed', with two 'Reviewed and adopted by' lines (Daniel Price, Ruth Price) and a total of $22,590. That total includes the coin collection twice ($2,500 + $2,500) and the Jaguar twice ($6,000 + $6,000). At that moment 0 of 13 lines were reviewed, 0 were decided, all 7 rooms were pending, and Possible duplicates showed 0 groups. The Estate Inventory Report from the same state was stamped 'IN PROGRESS — 0 of 13 items reviewed', and the work bar says client documents print IN PROGRESS until every line is ticked. The Court Inventory carries no such stamp: in printCourtInventory, havellin.html:34030-34112, FINAL depends only on pending appraisals, unvalued lines and the matter. The proposal extends the existing DRAFT rule, which withholds only the signature block, and leaves 'not reviewed' out of its reasons, so it does not conflict with 'Review gates nothing'.

findings.title: One snapshot of a full house pushes the job record past the Jobs sheet's 50,000-character cell
findings.where: More ▾ > Snapshot. takeInventorySnapshot havellin.html:30265 (job.invSnapshots.push with every line, shaped by _snapItemOf at 30262). Server: saveAllJobsToSheet apps-script/main-sync.gs:1477-1525 clears every data row (1520), then writes all jobs in one setValues. The cap is noted at main-sync.gs:615.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/INV/run3.js, through the real More > Snapshot (label 'Filed with court'), 400 named lines: the job JSON went from 1,344 to 58,402 characters, and the saveAllJobs payload that followed was 62,106 characters. A Google Sheets cell holds 50,000. BUILD_HISTORY.md:29 records the team's own finding that a Jobs cell over 50,000 characters 'can leave the tab empty'. The server half is reasoning from the code: Apps Script cannot run here.
findings.tc_impact: The playbook tells the TC a snapshot is 'your amended-inventory trail' (concierge-guide.html:992). One press on a normal-sized estate and every later job write from that device fails, and the outbox retries it forever; the clear before the write may empty the Jobs tab for every client. Nothing reaches counsel and the job is stuck.
findings.proposal: Keep the snapshot's lines off the job record. Store items in the job's MediaStore entry (already chunked at 45,000) or file them to Drive as JSON beside the inventory, keeping {ts, label, count, totalFMV, valueDate, itemsRef} on the job. Add an app-side guard that refuses, by name, to queue any job record over 45,000 characters. Check row sizes before clearContent in saveAllJobsToSheet, so one oversized row can never empty the tab.
findings.vnote: One real More ▾ > Snapshot press on a 400-line named estate took the job record from 1,344 to 54,642 characters. Each snapshot line keeps itemNo, object, category, fmv, disposition and track. Both writes that followed carried the whole row: saveAllJobs (body 54,677) and the per-job write (54,667). Both are over the 50,000-character cell cap, and havellin.html has no size guard. The server half is code reading; Apps Script cannot run here. saveAllJobsToSheet clears every data row before one setValues (main-sync.gs:1519-1520), and BUILD_HISTORY.md:29 records the team's own finding that a Jobs cell over 50,000 'can leave the tab empty'. Even without that, every later saveAllJobs from that device carries the oversized row, so all of its job writes fail and retry for good. A 200-line house with two snapshots crosses the cap too.

findings.title: A walkthrough collection photographed as an ordinary item is on every paper twice, and the desk shows it only inside the line's record
findings.where: collectionLinesEnsure havellin.html:35979 makes the line with roomIdx null. _agDupEligible 37954 and _arCheckable 38207 require a room, so agentDuplicateGroups (38006) and the room check never see it. The only join is the record's picker (_collPanelHtml, ~36100). _agShotPayload/_agContext (37586, 37618) send Agent One no collections.
findings.evidence: INV/run1.js and run2.js; pages in INV/out1/court.html and INV/out2/eir.html. Setup: estimate collection 'Coin collection' ($3,000, appraise); Agent One named photo s25 'Coin collection in three blue albums'. Possible duplicates: 0 groups. The Court Inventory lists 'Coin collection, as photographed, not stated, $3,000' and 'Coin collection in three blue albums … $3,000', Collectibles subtotal $6,000. The Estate Inventory Report lists both. The summary shows Collectibles 2 / $6,000, and the MAIV aggregate '8 articles … $13,060' counts both. The living Contents Record (run7.js, out7/contents.html) lists both. The only cue on the row is a '📷 no photograph yet' chip whose explanation is a tooltip, which an iPad cannot show.
findings.tc_impact: The TC must remember every walkthrough collection, open each unshot line's record and find the twin in a dropdown of every line on the job (400 on a full house). Missed, the reader receives a $3,000 double and a wrong §20.2031-6(b) aggregate on a schedule that can go FINAL (INV-01).
findings.proposal: Send the open walkthrough collections and vehicles (id, name, category) in _agContext, and let record_objects return walkthrough: <id> when an object is one of them. The desk then raises it in Possible duplicates as 'From the walkthrough: is #20 the Coin collection?' with Use that line (one press, already built) and 'Not the same'. As a fallback that needs no agent, agentDuplicateGroups joins an unshot collection line with a photographed line of the same category that shares a name word. Until it is photographed or matched, an unshot collection line prints its figure as 'walkthrough estimate, not yet photographed', and the schedules stay DRAFT (INV-01).
findings.vnote: Reproduced. Estimate collection 'Coin collection' ($2,500); Agent One named photo b1 'Coin collection in red binders'. Agent One's request context carried categories, conditions, mustFind, fiduciary and matterType, and no collections or vehicles. Possible duplicates showed 0 groups: the collection line has no room, and _agDupEligible and _arCheckable both require one. The Court Inventory printed both lines at $2,500. The row's bronze '📷 no photograph yet' chip is visible, but its explanation is a tooltip (title attribute); the join is Use that line inside the record. Re-rated from fix-now to high: the join is built and the row does flag the line. What is missing is detection, and INV-01's gate is where the paper goes wrong. Sibling, new: the unshot collection line prints condition 'as photographed' on the Court Inventory with no photograph behind it ('Coin collection as photographed not stated $2,500').
findings.vrepro: INV-verify/v1.js → v1.log (agentIdentify context keys, dup groups []); INV-verify/v2.log coin rows; havellin.html:37954, 38207, 39703-39707

findings.title: The walkthrough's vehicle Add makes a second line for a car already photographed in the garage, and nothing joins them
findings.where: Panel 'From the Estimate Walkthrough' > Add →. materializeVehicle havellin.html:36189; _importedSourceSet 35930 counts only lines carrying sourceVehId; no vehicle equivalent of collectionUseLine.
findings.evidence: INV/run4.js, section A. After the garage photo was named '1998 Mercedes-Benz SL500 convertible, silver' (#30, $14,000), the panel still offered '1998 Mercedes SL500 · vehicle Add →'. Pressing it made #51 '1998 Mercedes SL500' with no room and no photo. Possible duplicates showed 0 groups, and the Court Inventory then printed both ('$14,000 || Mercedes SL500 as photographed PR estimate $800').
findings.tc_impact: The panel asks the TC to press Add, a natural step at the start of the job; the car is then counted twice on the court schedule, usually one of the larger single values in the house.
findings.proposal: While a live Vehicles & Watercraft line exists, the panel's row asks 'Is #30 this vehicle? Use that line / Add it' instead of offering a bare Add. Use that line puts sourceVehId on the photographed line and fills its name and collector flag where blank. Agent One's walkthrough match (INV-03) does it with no press.
findings.vnote: Reproduced. After the garage photo was named '1987 Jaguar XJ6 sedan, red' (#11, $6,000), the panel still read 'From the Estimate Walkthrough (1 to add) … 1987 Jaguar XJ6 · vehicle … Add →'. Pressing it made #14 '1987 Jaguar XJ6' with no room and no photograph, and Possible duplicates showed 0 groups. The Court Inventory then printed both lines at $6,000. materializeVehicle guards only on sourceVehId (_importedSourceSet), and nothing like collectionUseLine exists for vehicles. The hand-added line also prints 'as photographed' with no photograph.

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 (P8, its critical part: Not duplicates recorded for the pair, dupOKIn since its review (one id per press on every line of the group), agentDupCleared; the room check counts only a double the block shows; tests/p8-nothing-twice.test.js, browser step 123)
findings.title: Not duplicates silences a line for good: a later real double of it is stamped but never shown
findings.where: Possible duplicates > Not duplicates. agentNotDuplicate havellin.html:38121 sets dupOK on every line of the group; _arDupEligible 38082 and _agDupEligible 37954 skip any dupOK line whoever it is paired with; the room-check state line counts doubles written, not doubles shown.
findings.evidence: INV/run9.js. The room check flags sofa #1 with armchair #10 (low); Not duplicates leaves 0 groups. Next, a new Items photo s99 of the same sofa is added; the work bar offers 'Check 1 room'; the room check answers s00+s99 'high'. The lines then read s00 dupWith=['s99'] dupOK=true and s99 dupWith=['s00']. The work bar says 'Room check: 1 possible double flagged under Possible duplicates', and Possible duplicates shows 0 groups.
findings.tc_impact: The TC is told a double is flagged and cannot find it; the sofa stays on the list twice. Every 'not duplicates' answer on a pair blinds the check for those lines for the rest of the job.
findings.proposal: Record Not duplicates per pair: agentNotDuplicate writes dupOKWith (the stableIds of the group's other lines) on each line, and agentDuplicateGroups drops a link only when the pair is on that list. A room-check link to any other line shows as usual. _arStateHtml counts the groups the panel will show.
findings.vnote: Reproduced with my own room-check stub. Round 1 flagged sofa a0 with club chair a2 (low), and Not duplicates left 0 groups with dupOK=1 on both lines. Then one new unnamed Items photo a9 went into the Living Room; Name 1 shot named it, and the automatic room check flagged a0+a9 'high'. Result: a0 dupWith=['a9'] dupOK=true, a9 dupWith=['a0'] dupOK=false. The work bar read 'Room check: 1 possible double flagged under Possible duplicates', while the panel showed 0 groups and agentDuplicateGroups returned 0. _arWrite never clears dupOK, and _arDupEligible skips any dupOK line whatever it is paired with.

findings.title: No room-by-room completeness readout; a room with no lines disappears from the desk and from every paper
findings.where: The desk groups by disposition, then room (_invGroupItems), and the room filter lists only rooms with lines (_renderInvFilterRow 39511). The summary (_renderInventorySummary 29364) has no completeness rows. The Estate Inventory Report, Court Inventory, Trust Schedule and Contents Record print only rooms that hold lines. lockRefusal 41388 locks a room with no Items photo. The Job Plan's room list has 'N found · N items · N after' (41623); the desk has nothing like it.
findings.evidence: INV/seed.js: 8 rooms in scope; the Study has an as-found shot and no Items; the Hall Closet has nothing. run4.js E: 'Study:pending:items=0:asfound=1 | Hall Closet:pending:items=0:asfound=0'. 'Study' and 'Hall Closet' each appear 0 times in out2/eir.html, out1/court.html, out4/court-final.html and out7/contents.html; only out2/asfound.html names the Hall Closet. The summary (run2.js) reports Total Items 50 and Items Awaiting Valuation 1, and nothing per room.
findings.tc_impact: The TC cannot drive the list to green before it goes to counsel. They have to check the Job Plan's room list against the desk from memory, and nothing totals named, reviewed, valued, decided and checked per room. The reader cannot tell an empty room from one never inventoried. The executor's completeness statement under §20.2031-6(b) has nothing to rest on.
findings.proposal: A DOM-free inventoryCompleteness(jobId, job, all) and a 'Ready for counsel' card at the head of tonight's items. One row per room in scope: as-found (shots, pass ticked), Items photos, lines, unnamed, nothing to list, not reviewed, no value or no basis (on tiers that state values), undecided, room check ('checked' or 'N to check'), duplicates open, status (pending, locked, cleared). Each count is a press that filters to those lines (the existing _invFilter.flag plus room). Job-wide rows: walkthrough collections and vehicles unmatched, must-finds unreconciled (INV-11), lots over the cap (INV-09). A locked room with no lines reads 'nothing inventoriable, locked <day> by <who>': Lock is already the attestation, so no new box. Print the same table as a 'Rooms inventoried' index on the Estate Inventory Report, Court Inventory and Trust Schedule, and let the package's gap question (INV-07) and the schedules' DRAFT rule (INV-01) read it.
findings.vnote: Accurate. In my run the Study (as-found only) and the Hall Closet (nothing) each appear 0 times on the Court Inventory and the Estate Inventory Report; only the As-Found Record names them (1 each). The Court Inventory has no room column at all. lockRefusal (havellin.html:41388) asks only for an as-found shot and the pass tick, never an Items photo or a line. The desk has no per-room counts. The proposal derives everything from records already kept, adds no box, and does not conflict with a Decided item. Kept at high because it underpins INV-01 and INV-07; nothing on a paper is wrong because of it alone.

findings.title: The package's gap question ignores unnamed lines: a house of 31 unnamed shots reads as one line short
findings.where: probatePackageGaps havellin.html:17698 counts named lines only, and its 'live' list requires an objectName. The confirm put before the estate package is drafted reads it.
findings.evidence: INV/run8.js, before Name shots: probatePackageGaps → ['8 rooms not yet locked','1 line with no disposition'] while 31 lines were unnamed. The one named line was the walkthrough collection's own line, made by itself; that also satisfies probatePackageInventoryBlocker's 'a named live line', so the package can be drafted from this state.
findings.tc_impact: The one question that is meant to make an interim package deliberate tells the TC the inventory is nearly finished; counsel receives pages full of blank rows.
findings.proposal: probatePackageGaps reads the completeness reader (INV-06): 'N photographs not yet named', 'N with nothing to list', 'N possible duplicates open', 'N lines not reviewed', the rooms not locked, and on value tiers 'N with no value'. probatePackageInventoryBlocker should not count a walkthrough line that has never been photographed as the inventory.
findings.vnote: Reproduced before any naming, on an activated estate with 12 unnamed Items lines. probatePackageGaps returned ['7 rooms not yet locked','1 line with no disposition'], counting only named lines. probatePackageInventoryBlocker returned '' (pass) because the one named line is the walkthrough collection's own line, which the app makes by itself. So the guard added on 2026-10-19 after a blank-floor package went out ('no named live line') is defeated whenever the estimate carries a collection.

findings.title: A photograph Agent One found nothing in stays a live line: it prints as a blank row on the Court Inventory and keeps it in DRAFT
findings.where: agentApplyResult havellin.html:37676-37688 stamps agentConf 'none' and keeps the line. The Unnamed shots chip tests !r.objectName (37091). _invScheduleSection 33978 and the Estate Inventory Report's itemRow (31054) print the line.
findings.evidence: INV/run1.js: sock-drawer photo s32 (empty answer) became #23. Chips: 'Unnamed shots 1 … No value yet 1'. The Court Inventory row reads '— as photographed not stated —', and the status 'DRAFT — 4 items pending appraisal · 1 item not yet valued' with the floor note '#23 unnamed' (out1/court.html). Estate Inventory Report row: '23 — Kitchen 1 as photographed — not stated' (out2/eir.html). Contents Record: '1 photographed item not yet named' (run7.js). Removing one takes 4 presses (run4.js C).
findings.tc_impact: Agent One is right to leave out sock drawers, packaging and bare surfaces, and on a 400-photo house that can be dozens of photographs. Each one still costs 4 presses, or the court schedule carries blank rows and stays DRAFT for a reason the TC must decode ('#23 unnamed').
findings.proposal: Treat agentConf 'none' as the photograph's answer, not a line. Leave it out of the papers, the counts, Not reviewed and the summary; it stays in the room's photo strip as the record. The naming state line ('1 with nothing in frame') carries one press: 'Remove the N with nothing to list' (one bulk tombstone with the reason, restorable from Removed items). A name typed into one brings it back as a line.
findings.vnote: Reproduced. Photo a3 got an empty answer and stayed live line #4, whose row reads 'nothing to list'. Before cleaning, the Court Inventory was 'DRAFT — … 1 item not yet valued' with the floor note '#4 unnamed' and one blank '— as photographed … —' row. Removing it took 4 presses (Unnamed shots chip, ▾, Remove line, confirm). Re-rated to medium. The DRAFT it causes is safe rather than wrong, and the field guide keeps most such frames out of the Items pass. The cost is presses and a blank row on the IN PROGRESS Estate Inventory Report. On the proposal, prefer the one-press recorded removal: leaving lines off papers by rule edges on 'Removal is a recorded act, never an absence'.
findings.vrepro: INV-verify/v5.log (INV-08 court lines), INV-verify/v2.log (a3 row, presses); havellin.html:37676-37688

findings.title: On a Form 706 estate a mixed group at qty 1 escapes the $100 lot test, and the worklist prints a clearance
findings.where: invLotSplitState havellin.html:28176 answers '' when qty is not above 1. _lotSplitWorklistBlock 35234 takes lots as qty > 1 and prints the clearance at 35264. Agent One's prompt (main-sync.gs:3348-3368) makes a mixed group one line of qty 1.
findings.evidence: INV/run5.js (706 = yes). With every qty>1 lot at $90 an article, the Appraisal Worklist printed: '9 lines on this manifest group more than one article under a single value. Every grouped lot averages below $100 an article, so §20.2031-6(a) permits them to stand as groups on the return schedule.' At the same time #25 'Jewelry box contents: rings, brooches, wristwatches' (qty 1, $1,800) and #22 'Kitchen drawer contents: utensils, tape, batteries, string' (qty 1, $150) stood as single lines. Neither the Lots to split chip nor the worklist names them. #19 'Sterling silver flatware service, Gorham' (named with no count, $2,400) is invisible to the test too.
findings.tc_impact: The TC is told the return's grouping is clean while a $1,800 box of jewelry sits as one line; the accountant or the IRS meets the lump. The research notes list exactly this as a classic failure (R1-standards.md:135).
findings.proposal: record_objects returns group: true for any line that holds more than one article, mixed or of one kind; _agWrite stores it, and the desk shows it in the record. invLotSplitState answers 'check' for a group line whose count is 1 or not given and whose value is over $100. The chip and the worklist then name it: 'a grouped lot with no count: itemise it, or record on the line why it is properly grouped'. The clearance sentence prints only when nothing is in 'check', and says 'no article recorded above $100' rather than 'permits them to stand'.
findings.vnote: The code confirms it: invLotSplitState returns '' unless qty > 1, and _lotSplitWorklistBlock takes lots as qty > 1, so its clearance sentence ignores qty-1 groups. Observed: my 'Sideboard drawer contents: candles, napkin rings, coasters, corkscrews' (qty 1, $180) is absent from the worklist's lot block and the Lots to split chip, which counted 2. Re-rated to medium. The auditor's headline case, a $1,800 qty-1 jewelry box, is a state Agent One's prompt forbids: jewelry gets a line of its own and is taken out of mixed groups (main-sync.gs:3343-3368). The realistic residue is a mixed everyday group over $100 printed under a clearance sentence that never tested it.

findings.title: Must-finds are ticked found without naming the item, and an unfound one is on no paper, at the close or in the package
findings.where: The desk brief's Found it: toggleMustFound havellin.html:10963 records mustFound[key] = {at, by} only. mustFindItems is read only by the brief (10388-10420), Agent One's context (37622) and the notice rule (37873).
findings.evidence: INV/run4.js, section B. Must-find list: 'Grandmother's diamond engagement ring / Father's Rolex Submariner / The deed box', none photographed. findings.tc_impact: Nobody can later show where the ring went, or that the Rolex was never found. The attorney is not told the family's must-finds were missing, which is the first question a beneficiary asks.
findings.proposal: Found it opens a one-line picker: 'Which item? #… / handed to the family / not inventory'. It stores the stableId. Agent One's mustfind notice carries which (an enum over the unfound list it is already sent), so the notice's 'This is it' records the match with its line in one press. The package's confirm and the Estate Inventory Report print 'Items the family asked us to find: ring, #25; Rolex, not found'. An unfound must-find is named in the close's question (a flag, never a refusal).
findings.vnote: Reproduced. One press of Found it on the desk's must-find host recorded {"mother's pearl necklace":{"at":…,"by":"Ashley Jerome"}} with no dialog and no item. closeOpenWorkFlag, jobCloseBlockers, probatePackageDocs and printEstateInventoryReport contain no must-find reader (grep count 0 each). The list is read only by the brief, Agent One's context and the notice rule. Re-rated to medium: this is a gap in the record, not a wrong paper. findings.title: The room check reads every photograph of a room with its lines, but is told not to report what no line names

findings.tc_impact: The TC is the only check on under-listing, at 72-240 px thumbnails, line by line. The reader receives a list that is short with no sign of it, the case a twenty-year appraiser walking the room would catch.
findings.proposal: Add unlisted: [{photo label, what, confidence}] to record_doubles: 'a thing plainly in a photograph that no line from any of the room's photographs names'. It rides the same call with no new images. The desk lists them under Possible duplicates as 'Possibly not on the list: a cobalt vase on the coffee table (photo of #4)', with + Add line (a blank line on that photo, which Name shots fills under the listed rule) and Not inventory.

Only lines count.' record_doubles has only lines, why and confidence (apps-script/main-sync.gs:3786-3842). Whether a real model would usefully report unlisted objects cannot be tested here. Caution: the proposal adds a new flag kind to clear, which pulls against Anthony's 2026-10-25b 'I don't want them … sending up a bunch of flags that need to be cleared'. It must also respect Agent One's background rule, so the table under the subject is not raised as missing. Not on the Decided list, but Anthony should be asked before it is built.

findings.title: KNOWN: the room check reads 38% of photo pairs in a 40-photo room, and the name rule is exact and per room
findings.where: _arWindows apps-script/main-sync.gs:3776 (AGENT_ROOM_WINDOW 12, OVERLAP 6); agentDuplicateGroups havellin.html:38030 keys the name rule on roomIdx + name; evening-desk-guide.html:406.
findings.evidence: KNOWN: in P24's 'found in passing' items: one room at a time, and pairs more than six apart can miss. New impact, measured by INV/window.js against the server's own windows: 100% of pairs at 12 photos, 80% at 16, 61% at 24, 38% at 40, 27% at 60. Two run1 cases produced no group. The sofa, photographed 13 shots apart in a 14-photo living room under two names. And the identical 'Brass table lamps with pleated shades' (qty 2) in the living and dining rooms. The Evening Desk says the room check 'flags anything photographed twice in a room'.
findings.tc_impact: A Palm Beach living room is 30-60 photos, so most pairs in the rooms that matter are never compared. The TC trusts a clean Possible duplicates panel that has not looked.
findings.proposal: 1. A text-only pass across the whole house: every line's name, category, qty and room in one request, with no images (hundreds of lines fit), answering candidate pairs. Then a vision check on only those pairs' photos, which is the existing room check with a two-photo run. 2. Widen the name rule to identical name and qty across rooms. 3. The Evening Desk says 'compares photos in overlapping batches', as the photography guide already does.
findings.vnote: Open work, 'P24, found in passing': the check reads one room at a time, and in a room of more than 12 photographs, shots more than six apart can miss each other and twelve or more apart always do. The new arithmetic is right: I recomputed it against _arWindows' half-open runs and got 100%, 80%, 61%, 38% and 27% of pairs read together at 12, 16, 24, 40 and 60 photos. The Evening Desk sentence, 'flags anything photographed twice in a room' (evening-desk-guide.html:406), is new and belongs with INV-22. Proposal 2 (the same name and qty across rooms) would flag genuine matched pairs, such as two pairs of lamps in two rooms, against the room check's own 'matching things are separate' rule.
findings.vrepro: python recomputation against apps-script/main-sync.gs:3775-3785 (AGENT_ROOM_WINDOW 12, OVERLAP 6); evening-desk-guide.html:406

findings.title: A snapshot keeps only number, name, category, value and disposition, so a count, room or basis change after it is invisible
findings.where: _snapItemOf havellin.html:30262; snapshotDiff 30314; printInventorySnapshot.
findings.evidence: INV/run5.js: snapshot 'Delivered to counsel', then the appraised ginger jars' Qty typed 2 → 3 on the row (the appraised value stays $700). Compare with now read 'Items 50 → 50 … Unchanged 50'. run2.js printed the snapshot item's keys: itemNo, object, category, fmv, disposition, track.
findings.tc_impact: The playbook sells the snapshot as the amended-inventory trail. A corrected count, a line moved to another room, or a basis replaced by an appraisal after delivery never shows on the comparison counsel would rely on.
findings.proposal: Add qty, roomIdx, condition, valSource/valuedBy, valDate and the photo's file id to _snapItemOf. snapshotDiff compares them under three new headings: Count changed, Moved room, Basis changed. Store the lines off the job (INV-02).
findings.vnote: Reproduced. I took a real Snapshot ('Delivered to counsel'), then typed Qty 2 → 3 on the appraised line's row; its value stayed $700 as an appraisal. Compare with now then read 'Items 400 → 400 … Value changed 0 … Unchanged 400' (and the same at 40 lines). The snapshot keeps only itemNo, object, category, fmv, disposition and track, and snapshotDiff compares only object, fmv, disposition and track. Not compared: count, room, condition, and a change of basis.

findings.title: Nothing records what the adopted Court Inventory covered or what has changed since, so the supplementary inventory is left to memory
findings.where: signedScheduleRows havellin.html:35167 (an adopted copy records kind and ref only); no supplementary-inventory document anywhere in havellin.html.
findings.evidence: Code reading: filing the adopted copy takes no snapshot and records no lines; a grep finds no supplementary or amended inventory. The research notes (audit/research/R1-standards.md:26) cite §733.604(2) and Rule 5.340: an amendment is owed when property is found missing, when a value or description proves erroneous, or when an unknown value is later determined.
findings.tc_impact: Something found in a closet after the PR adopted the schedule, or a value an appraisal later replaces, has to be remembered by the TC and redone by counsel from the full list.
findings.proposal: Filing the adopted Court Inventory (or the received Trust Schedule) takes a snapshot by itself, labelled with that paper and stored off the job. The Closing bar's line then reads 'Supplement owed: 3 added, 2 values changed since the Court Inventory adopted Nov 4', and offers a Supplementary Inventory built from snapshotDiff: added lines in full, changed lines as was and now, with its own adoption lines.
findings.vnote: Accurate. signedScheduleRows records only the paper (kind and ref). Filing the adopted copy takes no snapshot, and no supplementary or amended inventory exists anywhere in havellin.html (grep). §733.604(2) does call for an amended or supplementary inventory when property is found or a value or description proves erroneous. Counsel files it, so this is a support gap, not a wrong paper.

findings.title: Lots to split has no way to split a lot, and Agent One cannot help
findings.where: INV_WORK_FLAGS 'lotsplit' havellin.html:37105 is a chip only, with no hint on the row or in the record. invSplitItemN 28749 adds one blank line per press. agentListedOff 37600 and _agListedText main-sync.gs:3528 ('Never record a listed object again').
findings.evidence: INV/run1.js: Lots to split 3: #16 eight chairs at $200 each, #29 six prints at $150, #7 two jars at $350. The rows and records give no reason. By the code (not observed live), to itemise the chairs: 7 presses of + Another item in this photo. Name shots then sends the photo with 'Set of 8 mahogany dining chairs (qty 8)' listed and the instruction to record only what is not listed, so the answer is empty and the seven blank lines read nothing to list. findings.tc_impact: On a 706 estate every set of chairs, service of china or group of prints over $100 an article is a manual rebuild.
findings.proposal: 'Itemise into N' on a lot's record and on the bulk bar. It makes N lines of qty 1 sharing the photo, each with the lot's name, Each (the value over N), destination and condition, numbered next, and tombstones the lot as 'itemised into #…'. Agent Two then re-values each as research. Show the lot's sentence (invLotSplitSentence) on the row.
findings.vnote: Accurate. Lots to split is a chip only. invLotSplitSentence is defined but read by nothing: grep finds only its definition, despite its comment naming the desk. Pressing + Another item in this photo on the 6-chair lot added a blank #14 and a toast. Name 1 shot then sent b0 with listed:[{name:'Carved oak dining chairs', qty:6}], and the server prompt says 'Never record a listed object again … record an empty list'. My stub does not honour that rule, so the empty answer is reasoning from the prompt text. No itemise or split-into-N control exists.

findings.title: A count in a name is never caught at the desk, and a corrected count then contradicts it on the schedule
findings.where: AGENT_COUNT_IN_NAME_RE apps-script/main-sync.gs:3527 is read only by the probes' log lines (3717, 4953); there is no check in the app.
findings.evidence: INV/run1.js: 'Set of 8 mahogany dining chairs' (qty 8) and 'Pair of Chinese porcelain ginger jars' were written as named. INV/run8.js: Qty typed 8 → 6 on the row; the Court Inventory row became 'Set of 8 mahogany dining chairs (6 items, valued as a lot) … $1,200'.

findings.proposal: Lift the regex into the app. A line whose name matches shows a 'count in the name' hint on the row, with a one-press 'Take it out' ('Set of 8 mahogany dining chairs' → 'Mahogany dining chairs'). Agent Two's name rule strips a count on ordinary lots too, not only on lots it researches.
findings.vnote: Reproduced. 'Pair of Staffordshire spaniels' came back as named. Its row shows no hint, and after Qty was typed 1 the line read 'Pair of Staffordshire spaniels qty=1 fmv=250'. AGENT_COUNT_IN_NAME_RE is read only by the two probes' log lines (main-sync.gs:3717, 4953) and nowhere in the app. Low, because the prompt already bars counts in names.

findings.title: Folding an over-split drawer back into one group line takes 13 presses and a retyped name
findings.where: Bulk bar: Remove lines (invBulkRemove) is the only tool; there is no combine.
findings.evidence: INV/run8.js: Agent One listed a junk drawer as 12 lines (#21, #40-#50, $60 each, $720 on the schedule). Folding it took 11 ticks + Remove lines + confirm (13 presses), and the survivor 'Scissors' still had to be renamed as the group and re-valued by hand.
findings.tc_impact: It is rare after the 2026-10-19 prompt rules, but when it happens it costs a dozen presses and leaves the survivor's value and name wrong until fixed.
findings.proposal: 'Combine into one line' on the bulk bar for lines off one photo. It keeps the first number and names it '<room> drawer contents: scissors, tape measure, batteries…' (editable); qty is 1 for a mixed group or the sum for one kind; it marks the line as a group and runs Re-value. The rest are tombstoned 'combined into #21'.
findings.vnote: Accurate. The bulk bar has Re-value and Remove lines and no combine control (havellin.html:40164-40172; grep finds no combine or itemise button). The press count is from the auditor's run and consistent with the controls. It is rare since the 2026-10-19 drawer rule.
